reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it documents an unsuccessful attempt to reach CitiBank Costco support, with a standard hold message and an ongoing call shown on the phone. The described material contains no observable offer, payment or credential request, or investment claim.

citations.quote: CitiBank Costco non- support
Over an hour and 15 minutes still no one answers
All associates are currently assisting other customers.

opening.argument: The material presents continued holding as the necessary action for obtaining assistance: the caller is told to remain on the line until an associate becomes available. That creates a concrete action-outcome linkage, while the recording provides no evidence that assistance actually occurs. The unusually prolonged wait described alongside the hold instruction makes the promised service outcome difficult to verify and leaves open whether the interaction is functioning as an exploitative low-barrier acquisition funnel rather than ordinary support.

citations.quote: Please continue to hold and we will be with you as soon as the next associate is available.
Over an hour and 15 minutes still no one answers

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a support attempt does not resolve the central concern: the supplied account shows prolonged compliance with an instruction to keep holding, but no completed assistance. The title identifies a bank-related support context, yet a title alone does not establish that the purported service interaction is genuine or effective. The phone image shows an ongoing call, not a successful resolution.

citations.quote: CitiBank Costco non- support
Over an hour and 15 minutes still no one answers
Please continue to hold

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The argument stretches a hold instruction into a reward or acquisition promise that is never stated. The message identifies routine queue status and says an associate will respond when available; it does not request payment, credentials, registration, or any other qualifying action. An unanswered call may be frustrating, but these materials do not show a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: All associates are currently assisting other customers.
we will be with you as soon as the next associate is available.

opening.argument: The strongest risk signal is the combination of extreme duration and an unresolved demand for continued compliance. The description says the caller has waited more than an hour and fifteen minutes, while the recorded message still directs the caller to hold. That pairing supports a deceptive interpretation: the user is induced to keep investing time without any demonstrated result. The handset display confirms that a live call is being maintained, but does not verify who is receiving it or what outcome will follow.

citations.quote: Over an hour and 15 minutes still no one answers
Please continue to hold

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of an answer is precisely the risk signal, not evidence that the interaction is harmless. A generic automated message can be used to normalize indefinite waiting, and the footage supplies no independent confirmation that a legitimate representative will ever intervene. The ordinary-service framing therefore cannot by itself eliminate the possibility of deceptive retention.

citations.quote: All associates are currently assisting other customers.
still no one answers

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are inconvenience signals, not scam-specific signals. The recording gives a conventional explanation for the delay and a conditional expectation of assistance. Nothing in the supplied text or frames shows a reward, payment demand, credential collection, external link, investment, or other deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: All associates are currently assisting other customers.
we will be with you as soon as the next associate is available.

opening.argument: Although presented as a complaint about customer support, the video repeatedly centers the viewer's attention on maintaining the call and waiting for access to a service. That framing can function as promotion of a purported access pathway: it encourages viewers to accept prolonged compliance as the route to an eventual benefit, despite the material showing no completed assistance. The title's bank-and-Costco framing supplies an ordinary-commerce appearance, but the observable content remains an unresolved call rather than proof of legitimate service delivery.

citations.quote: CitiBank Costco non- support
Over an hour and 15 minutes still no one answers

rebuttal.rebuttal: The complaint framing does not make the content neutral. By documenting the hold process and emphasizing the extraordinary wait, it directs attention toward the alleged support pathway while leaving its effectiveness unverified. The bank-related title establishes the setting claimed by the video, not the authenticity or safety of the interaction depicted.

citations.quote: CitiBank Costco non- support
Over an hour and 15 minutes still no one answers

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The material does not promote participation; it documents frustration with an unsuccessful support attempt. The only spoken instruction is an automated queue message, and no viewer is directed to buy, register, deposit, contact an outside party, or provide information. Recasting a failed service call as promotion adds an objective that the evidence does not show.
